ContractFieldIssue.description:
One closed-vocabulary issue observed for one known contract member (issue #75): WHERE, by
server-owned path, and WHAT, by server-owned code. Never why, never with what value.

Path.description: The known contract member the issue concerns.

ContractIssueCode.description:
The closed error vocabulary issue #75 allows for a KNOWN contract member. Every member of this
enum is server-owned; none of them carries, encodes, or implies any value the client sent.

ContractMappingDelta.description:
The before/after comparison of ONE known contract member across the request mapping
(issue #75, "comparaison avant/après uniquement pour les membres déjà définis dans le
contrat"). This is the signal Option 1 actually delivers: it separates case (b) - the client
declared something and the mapping lost it - from case (c) - the mapping kept everything and the
decision engine is what changed.

CountAfter.description: How many entries survived the mapping, under the same convention as Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDelta.CountBefore.

CountBefore.description:
How many entries the client declared for a collection member, or 0 for a scalar member (whose
signal is Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDelta.PresentBefore/Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDelta.PresentAfter instead).

Path.description: The known contract member this delta concerns.

PresentAfter.description: Whether the member survived into the mapped capabilities.

PresentBefore.description: Whether the member was declared by the client.

ContractMappingDiagnostic.description:
Issue #75, Option 1: what the server can honestly say about ONE playback request's journey
through the capability mapping, using a strictly closed, server-owned vocabulary.

Deltas.description:
The before/after comparison for the known contract members that LOST something across the
mapping. Only genuine losses are listed - a member that survived intact, or that grew (the
reverse mapper legitimately synthesizes per-codec entries from direct-play combinations),
produces no entry. Empty means the mapping preserved everything it is asked about, which points
at case (c).

FieldIssues.description:
Closed-vocabulary issues for known members. Empty in this iteration: see
Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractIssueCode for why each code either has no semantically correct source yet
or is structurally unobservable at this point in the pipeline. Present so the shape does not
have to change when one of them becomes truthfully emittable.

MappingVersion.description:
The server-side mapping version this diagnostic was produced under - a compile-time server
constant, never anything the client influences. Lets two diagnostics from different server
builds be told apart.

PayloadSizeBytes.description:
The total request payload size in bytes, read from the `Content-Length` header alone, or
null when the header is absent (a chunked or streamed request). Deliberately
System.Nullable`1: request buffering is NOT enabled to measure the body, so
"unknown" is reported as unknown rather than as a lying 0. A count of bytes, never a byte of
content.

StructuralScan.description:
Issue #75 slice 75b: the result of the bounded, single-pass structural scan of the raw request
body, or null when no scan ran for this diagnostic - which is the case for
every slice-75a-only diagnostic, and whenever the request was not sampled for scanning. Trailing
and nullable so every slice-75a call site and OpenAPI consumer keeps working unchanged; a
non-null value is the signal that the scan actually executed (a silently-disabled scan cannot
present one). Like the rest of this type, its entire closure is enums and integers - see
Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.

UnknownMemberTotal.description:
The count-shaped slot slice 75a leaves null: the 75a mapping comparison does
not read the raw body, so on a diagnostic that carries no Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDiagnostic.StructuralScan this is
honestly null (unknown, never a lying 0). Slice 75b's bounded structural scan reports its own
truthful total on Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.UnknownMemberTotal instead of mutating
this field, so every slice-75a assertion that this stays null keeps holding while the scanned
total is still available (on Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDiagnostic.StructuralScan) when a scan actually ran.

ContractMember.description:
One segment of a Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractPath: a member the SERVER declares in the playback
request contract, named by a server-owned enum rather than by any text the client sent
(issue #75, "chemins connus représentés par un enum interne au serveur, jamais par une chaîne
fournie par le client").

ContractPath.description:
A path to a known member of the playback request contract, expressed as a fixed-arity tuple of
server-owned Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMember segments (issue #75).

Branch.description: The middle segment, or Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMember.None for a one-segment path.

Leaf.description: The innermost segment, or Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMember.None for a shorter path.

ContractStructuralScan.description:
Issue #75 slice 75b: the result of the BOUNDED, SINGLE-PASS structural scan of ONE raw playback
request body - what the server can honestly count about members the client sent, without ever
materializing a key, a value, an excerpt, a truncated form, or a hash of any of them.

BodyLimitExceeded.description:
True when the request body exceeded the scan's explicit size limit, so the scan stopped without
producing counts. The bound is on how much the scan reads; model binding is unaffected and still
sees the whole body. Lets "the body was too large to scan" be told apart from "the body was
scanned and had no unknown members".

ScannedBodyByteCount.description:
The number of bytes the scan actually read from the request body. This is the honest measured
size when the `Content-Length` header was absent (a chunked/streamed request), where
Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDiagnostic.PayloadSizeBytes is null. A count of bytes, never a byte
of content. Null only if the body was not read (see Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.BodyLimitExceeded).

UnknownMemberTotal.description:
The total number of members the client sent, anywhere the scan looked, that the contract does
not declare. A count, never a name. 0 is meaningful here (unlike on
Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDiagnostic.UnknownMemberTotal): the scan actually ran, so "the
client sent no unknown members" is a fact the server can now establish rather than a lying zero.

UnknownMembers.description:
The per-container breakdown of Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.UnknownMemberTotal: one entry per known container
that had at least one unknown member directly inside it. Empty when
Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.UnknownMemberTotal is 0. The entries sum to Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractStructuralScan.UnknownMemberTotal.

WrongTypes.description:
Closed-vocabulary Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractIssueCode.WrongType issues for KNOWN members only: a
member the contract declares as numeric that arrived as a JSON string. The scan judges by JSON
token kind alone and never reads the string's content. Which of these actually SURVIVES to a
retained diagnostic is bounded by the binder: only a numeric-looking string (e.g. `"64000"`)
binds under `NumberHandling.AllowReadingFromString` and lets the request reach the shadow
publication point; a non-numeric string 400s at the binder, so its (leak-free) WrongType is
observed by the scan but never retained. Either way the operator learns only "a known numeric
member arrived string-typed under this path", never which value.

ContractUnknownMemberCount.description:
Issue #75 slice 75b: HOW MANY members the client sent that the contract does not declare, under
one known container named by a server-owned Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractPath - never WHICH members,
and never a single character of any of their names.

Count.description: How many unknown members appeared directly under Path. Always > 0 - a container with no unknown members produces no entry.

Path.description: The known container the unknown members appeared inside.

PlaySessionId.description:
Optional. The client-facing play session id. At most one session is kept per play session id:
creating with the same id again replaces that session's plan and request.

PlaybackAttemptId.description:
Issue #43. Optional, opaque, client-generated. The identifier of the playback ATTEMPT this
request belongs to — generated once by the client when it starts trying to play something, and
resent unchanged on every request of that attempt: `PlaybackInfo`, this `POST`, the
`PUT`, and any retry. A new attempt gets a new value; a retry inside the same attempt keeps
the old one.

Distinct from both neighbouring scopes and substitutable for neither. It is NOT the
`RequestId`/`TraceId` of issue #42, which is server-derived and changes on every
request. It is NOT Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.CreatePlaybackSessionRequest.PlaySessionId, which only exists
once a session does — i.e. after `PlaybackInfo` has already happened — and which survives
across several attempts. See `docs/observabilite-identifiants-correlation.md`.
Diagnostics only: never an authorization key, no access decision is derived from it, and it
replaces no existing access control. Validated for length and printability only (see
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackAttemptIdValidator); no structure is imposed and no meaning is read out of it.

DeviceProfile.description:
A Tesserafin.Model.Dlna.DeviceProfile represents a set of metadata which determines which content a certain device is able to play.


Specifically, it defines the supported <see cref="P:Tesserafin.Model.Dlna.DeviceProfile.ContainerProfiles">containers</see> and
<see cref="P:Tesserafin.Model.Dlna.DeviceProfile.CodecProfiles">codecs</see> (video and/or audio, including codec profiles and levels)
the device is able to direct play (without transcoding or remuxing),
as well as which <see cref="P:Tesserafin.Model.Dlna.DeviceProfile.TranscodingProfiles">containers/codecs to transcode to</see> in case it isn't.

Name.description: Gets or sets the name of this device profile. User profiles must have a unique name.

DiagnosticComparison.description:
The legacy-vs-v2 shadow comparison for a session's retained diagnostic (§4.3): what legacy (the
source of truth) actually decided, the v2 engine's own decision shape, and the heuristic
classification of how the two compare. PR114: Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.DiagnosticComparison.V2Method/Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.DiagnosticComparison.V2Output/
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.DiagnosticComparison.V2SelectedStreams/Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.DiagnosticComparison.V2Transforms were added so the admin diagnostics
UI can render a real "live legacy vs. v2 decision" comparison - before this, only v2's
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.Reasoning tree was exposed, never its concrete decision
shape (the parent Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail's own `Method`/`Output`/
`SelectedStreams`/`Transforms` are always legacy-sourced, per
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponseMapper - never v2's).

What the server should produce when it must transcode, in the client's preference order (index
0 = most preferred). Empty when the client declares no transcoding targets at all, in which case
the engine falls back to a named legacy default (see `PlaybackEngine`).

PlaybackDecisionDecodeCapabilities.description:
What a client can read as-is, expressed without DLNA vocabulary: declared direct-play
combinations, and the codecs/subtitle delivery decodable outside of those combinations, each
with the limits within which it is decodable. An inline, immutable snapshot: the full
capability set travels with the request instead of being referenced by a stored profile id, so
a decision is reproducible from the request alone (RFC PR91 §4, option A).

AudioCodecs.description: The audio codecs the client can decode, and their limits.

DirectPlayProfiles.description:
The direct-play combinations the client declares, in declared order. Distinct from
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.DecodeCapabilities.VideoCodecs/Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.DecodeCapabilities.AudioCodecs: those describe per-codec decode limits
(used regardless of container), while this describes which container+codec(s) combinations are
actually playable together without transcoding (RFC PR102b problem #1).

SubtitleDelivery.description: The subtitle formats the client can render, and how it wants them delivered.

SupportsDash.description: Whether the client can play DASH renditions.

SupportsHls.description: Whether the client can play HLS renditions.

VideoCodecs.description: The video codecs the client can decode, and their limits.

PlaybackDecisionDecodeProfile.description:
One direct-play combination a client declares: this exact container packaged with this exact
video codec and this exact audio codec (for Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaKind.Video), or this exact
container with this exact audio codec (for Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaKind.Audio).

AudioCodecs.description:
The audio codecs this profile accepts. Empty is a wildcard (matches any audio codec), same
semantics as a legacy `DirectPlayProfile` with no `AudioCodec` declared.

Containers.description:
The containers this profile accepts. An empty list is a wildcard - matches any container -
same semantics as the legacy `DirectPlayProfile`, where an empty `Container` string
means unrestricted.

Type.description: Whether this profile is for audio-only or video (with or without audio) direct play.

VideoCodecs.description:
The video codecs this profile accepts. Empty is a wildcard (matches any video codec), same
semantics as a legacy `DirectPlayProfile` with no `VideoCodec` declared. Always empty
for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaKind.Audio profile.

PlaybackDecisionMediaKind.description: The kind of media being requested for playback.

PlaybackDecisionMediaSourceSnapshot.description:
A frozen snapshot of a media source, decoupled from any probing/model type. Carries no file
paths, URLs, or tokens: the domain performs no I/O (RFC PR91 §8, question 4).

AudioStreams.description: The audio streams on the source.

Bitrate.description: The overall source bitrate, or null if unknown.

MediaSourceId.description: The identifier of the source within its item.

RunTimeTicks.description: The runtime in ticks, or null if unknown.

SubtitleStreams.description: The subtitle streams on the source.

SupportsDirectPlay.description: Whether the source itself can be direct played, before client capabilities are considered.

SupportsDirectStream.description: Whether the source itself can be direct streamed (remuxed), before client capabilities are considered.

SupportsTranscoding.description: Whether the source itself can be transcoded.

VideoStreams.description: The video streams on the source.

PlaybackDecisionOutputSpec.description: The shape of the output a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision produces.

AudioBitrate.description:
The output audio stream's bitrate ceiling (PR103), or null if not
applicable/unbounded. Populated only when the audio is being transcoded, as the narrowest of the
used Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackOutputProfile.MaxAudioBitrate and the target codec's
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.AudioCodecCapability.MaxBitrate.

AudioChannels.description: The output audio channel count, or null if not applicable/unchanged.

AudioCodec.description: The normalized output audio codec, or null if not applicable.

Container.description: The normalized output container name, or null if not applicable.

Protocol.description:
The transport protocol this output is delivered over (PR102b). For Direct Play and Remux,
always Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.StreamingProtocol.Http - a protocol only diverges from plain HTTP when the
server produces the encoding, i.e. when transcoding to a client-declared
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackOutputProfile. Non-nullable: Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.StreamingProtocol.Http is the
neutral value for the "not applicable" case too, so this decision never leaves the delivery
protocol unstated.

Resolution.description: The output resolution, or null if not applicable/unchanged.

SubtitleFormat.description:
The format the client will actually receive the selected subtitle in, mirroring legacy
`StreamInfo.SubtitleFormat`, or null if not applicable/no subtitle
selected.

TotalBitrate.description:
The output's overall bitrate ceiling (PR103), or null if not
applicable/unbounded. Populated only when transcoding, as the narrowest of
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackConstraints.MaxBitrate (the request's global cap) and the sum of
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.OutputSpec.VideoBitrate/Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.OutputSpec.AudioBitrate when both are known - never a fabricated
value out of unknown per-stream ceilings.

VideoBitrate.description:
The output video stream's bitrate ceiling (PR103), or null if not
applicable/unbounded. Populated only when the video is being transcoded, as the narrowest of the
used Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackOutputProfile.MaxVideoBitrate and the target codec's
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.VideoCodecCapability.MaxBitrate.

VideoCodec.description: The normalized output video codec, or null if not applicable.

VideoRange.description: The normalized output video range type, or null if not applicable/unchanged.

PlaybackDecisionPlaybackConstraints.description:
The overrides and prohibitions attached to a playback request: what the caller allows or
prefers, independent of what the client or source are technically capable of.

AllowAudioStreamCopy.description: Whether the audio stream may be copied without re-encoding.

AllowDirectPlay.description: Whether direct play is permitted for this request.

AllowDirectStream.description: Whether direct stream (remux) is permitted for this request.

AllowTranscoding.description: Whether transcoding is permitted for this request.

AllowVideoStreamCopy.description: Whether the video stream may be copied without re-encoding.

AlwaysBurnInSubtitleWhenTranscoding.description: Whether subtitles must always be burned in whenever transcoding occurs, regardless of client subtitle capability.

MaxAudioChannels.description: The maximum audio channel count allowed, or null if unbounded.

MaxBitrate.description: The maximum overall bitrate allowed, or null if unbounded.

PreferredAudioStreamIndex.description: The preferred audio stream index, or null for no preference.

PreferredSubtitleLanguages.description:
The preferred subtitle languages, in preference order (PR103). An empty list is a wildcard -
matches any language - the same semantics as the legacy
`MediaStreamSelector.MatchesPreferredLanguage`.

PreferredSubtitleStreamIndex.description: The preferred subtitle stream index, or null for no preference.

StartTimeTicks.description: The playback start offset, in ticks.

SubtitleMode.description:
How to auto-select a subtitle stream (PR103) when PreferredSubtitleStreamIndex
is null - mirrors the legacy user-level `SubtitlePlaybackMode` preference
consumed by `MediaStreamSelector.GetDefaultSubtitleStreamIndex`.

PlaybackDecisionPlaybackMethod.description: The method by which the engine decided to deliver a media source to the client.

PlaybackDecisionPlaybackOutputProfile.description:
One target format the server can produce for this client when it must transcode, distinct from
what the client can already read as-is (Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.DecodeCapabilities). A client can declare
several of these on Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ClientCapabilities.OutputProfiles; their list order is the
client's preference order, most preferred first - PR102 exists precisely so that order survives
from the legacy `TranscodingProfile` list all the way to the engine, instead of being
collapsed into a flat capability set and replaced by hardcoded server-side preferences.

AudioCodecs.description: The target audio codecs, in the client's preference order (index 0 = most preferred).

Container.description: The target container for this output.

MaxAudioBitrate.description: The maximum audio bitrate for this output, or null if unbounded/unknown.

MaxAudioChannels.description: The maximum audio channel count for this output, or null if unbounded/unknown.

MaxVideoBitrate.description: The maximum video bitrate for this output, or null if unbounded/unknown.

Protocol.description: The streaming protocol this output is delivered over.

Type.description: Whether this profile targets audio-only or video output.

VideoCodecs.description:
The target video codecs, in the client's preference order (index 0 = most preferred). Empty for
an audio-only profile (Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackOutputProfile.Type of Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaKind.Audio).

PlaybackDecisionPlaybackRequestContext.description: The who/what/when of a playback request, independent of transport.

EngineVersion.description: The version of the decision engine that will produce (or produced) the decision for this request.

MediaKind.description: Whether audio or video playback is being requested.

MediaSourceId.description: The specific alternate source version requested, or null to let the engine choose.

RequestId.description: A unique identifier for this decision, for log/diagnostic correlation.

RequestedAt.description: The timestamp the request was made.

UserId.description: The requesting user, used for policy/quota purposes rather than technical selection.

PlaybackDecisionReasonCode.description:
A closed, stable, string-serialized reason code identifying a single leaf fact in a
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode tree. The constraint members mirror
`Tesserafin.Model.Session.TranscodeReason` one-to-one (that flags enum lists which walls a
legacy decision hit, without saying why); the positive/decision members and
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonCode.NoViablePlan have no legacy equivalent.

PlaybackDecisionReasonNode.description:
One node in the structured explanation tree for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision: what was
evaluated, what came of it, and (via Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode.Children) what sub-reasons led there. This
replaces a flat reason enum with causality: not just which walls were hit, but why the chosen
method follows from them.

Children.description: The sub-reasons that led to this node, or empty for a leaf.

Code.description: The stable, serializable reason code for this node.

Detail.description: Free-form detail (for example observed vs. expected values), or null if none.

Subject.description: What this node is reasoning about.

PlaybackDecisionReasonOutcome.description: The result a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode records for its Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonSubject.

PlaybackDecisionReasonSubject.description:
Identifies what a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode is talking about: a container, a specific
video/audio/subtitle stream, a source, or the playback method as a whole.

Kind.description: The kind of entity being referenced.

SourceId.description: The source identifier, when Kind is Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonSubjectKind.Source; otherwise null.

StreamIndex.description: The stream index, when Kind is Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonSubjectKind.VideoStream, Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonSubjectKind.AudioStream, or Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonSubjectKind.Subtitle; otherwise null.

PlaybackDecisionReasonSubjectKind.description: The kind of entity a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode is reasoning about.

PlaybackDecisionSelectedStreams.description: The video, audio, and subtitle streams selected for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision.

Audio.description: The selected audio stream index, or null if no audio stream was selected.

Subtitle.description: The selected subtitle stream and delivery method, or null if no subtitle was selected.

Video.description: The selected video stream index, or null if no video stream was selected.

PlaybackDecisionSelectedSubtitle.description: The subtitle stream selected for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision, and how it will be delivered.

Delivery.description: How the subtitle will be delivered to the client.

PlaybackDecisionStreamingProtocol.description:
The transport protocol an output stream is delivered over. Deliberately neutral vocabulary
(not `Tesserafin.Data.Enums.MediaStreamProtocol` or any other legacy/DLNA type): the domain
depends on nothing outside itself (RFC PR91 §4).

PlaybackDecisionSubtitleCapability.description: A subtitle format a client can render, and how it wants it delivered.

Method.description: The delivery method the client supports for this format.

PlaybackDecisionSubtitleDeliveryMethod.description: How a subtitle stream is delivered to the client.

PlaybackDecisionSubtitlePlaybackMode.description:
How a user wants subtitles auto-selected when no explicit stream index is requested. Mirrors
the legacy `Tesserafin.Database.Implementations.Enums.SubtitlePlaybackMode` (same member names
and numeric values) without depending on it: the domain assembly references nothing outside
itself (RFC PR91 §4/§7), so this is a domain-local copy of the vocabulary, not a reuse of the
legacy type.

PlaybackDecisionSubtitleStreamSnapshot.description:
A frozen snapshot of one subtitle stream on a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaSourceSnapshot, decoupled from
any probing/model type.

Index.description: The stream index within the source.

IsDefault.description: Whether this is the default subtitle stream on the source.

IsExternal.description: Whether the subtitle track is stored externally to the source.

IsForced.description: Whether the subtitle track is marked forced.

Language.description: The stream's language tag, or null if unknown.

PlaybackDecisionTransformKind.description:
A single transformation the playback pipeline must perform to realize a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision.
Orthogonal to Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackMethod: the method says which delivery strategy was chosen,
the transforms say what work that strategy actually requires of the pipeline.

PlaybackDecisionVideoCodecCapability.description: A video codec a client can decode, and the limits within which it can decode it.

MaxBitDepth.description: The highest bit depth the client supports, or null if unbounded/unknown.

MaxBitrate.description: The maximum video bitrate the client supports for this codec, or null if unbounded/unknown.

MaxLevel.description: The highest codec level the client supports, or null if unbounded/unknown.

MaxResolution.description: The maximum resolution the client supports for this codec, or null if unbounded/unknown.

Profiles.description: The codec profiles the client supports. Empty means no profile restriction is expressed.

VideoRangeTypes.description: The video range types (for example `"SDR"`, `"HDR10"`) the client supports for this codec.

PlaybackDecisionVideoStreamSnapshot.description:
A frozen snapshot of one video stream on a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaSourceSnapshot, decoupled from any
probing/model type.

BitDepth.description: The bit depth, or null if unknown.

Bitrate.description: The stream bitrate, or null if unknown.

Framerate.description: The framerate in frames per second, or null if unknown.

Height.description: The height in pixels, or null if unknown.

Index.description: The stream index within the source.

Level.description: The codec level, or null if unknown.

Profile.description: The codec profile, or null if unknown.

VideoRange.description: The video range type (for example `"SDR"`, `"HDR10"`), or null if unknown.

Width.description: The width in pixels, or null if unknown.

PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.description:
The richer, admin-only diagnostic projection of a tracked playback session
(docs/pr92-design-playback-api-and-diagnostics.md §4.3, PR113): every
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponse field, plus the request context, client capabilities,
source snapshot, full reasoning tree, and legacy/v2 comparison retained from a shadow run - when
one was retained at all.

Capabilities.description:
Everything the v2 engine needs to know about a requesting client: what it can decode as-is
(Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ClientCapabilities.Decode), and separately, what the server should produce when it must transcode
(Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ClientCapabilities.OutputProfiles).

Comparison.description: The legacy-vs-v2 shadow comparison, or null if no diagnostic was retained.

ContractMapping.description:
Issue #75 (Option 1): what the client's DECLARED capabilities lost on their way through the
request mapping, in a strictly closed server-owned vocabulary - or null when no
shadow diagnostic was retained (shadow mode is off by default), or when the session was planned
by a caller that declares no domain capabilities (the legacy path). Additive and nullable: a
client that ignores this member sees no change.

This member, unlike Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.Capabilities and Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.PlaybackAttemptId (both of which
intentionally echo client-supplied data and are catalogued as such in issue #80), cannot carry a
client-supplied value at all: its entire transitive type closure is enums, booleans and integers.
See Tesserafin.Playback.Contract.Diagnostics.ContractMappingDiagnostic for the closure guarantee and for an explicit account
of what Option 1 does NOT observe - unknown members above all.

CreatedAt.description: When the session was first created.

Kind.description: The kind of media being requested for playback.

LiveWiring.description:
PR115c: whether the live streaming path (`MediaInfoHelper.SetDeviceSpecificData`) actually
served this session from the v2 execution plan, or why it fell back to legacy - or
null when no live-wiring decision has been retained for this session yet
(request not yet made, or the session predates PR115c's diagnostics store). Independent of
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.Comparison: a session can have a shadow comparison retained without ever having
been through the live-wiring decision, and vice versa.

Method.description: The method by which the engine decided to deliver a media source to the client.

Output.description: The shape of the output a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision produces.

PlaybackAttemptId.description:
Issue #43: the opaque, client-supplied attempt id recorded on this session, or
null when the client sent none. This is the field that lets an operator pull up
every session — and therefore every retry — belonging to ONE playback attempt, which neither
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail.Id (per session) nor Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.DiagnosticTimelineEntry.RequestId (per request,
issue #42) can do. Opaque: displayed verbatim, never parsed.

Reasoning.description:
One node in the structured explanation tree for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision: what was
evaluated, what came of it, and (via Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonNode.Children) what sub-reasons led there. This
replaces a flat reason enum with causality: not just which walls were hit, but why the chosen
method follows from them.

Reasons.description: A flat summary of the reason codes behind this decision.

RequestContext.description: The who/what/when of a playback request, independent of transport.

SelectedStreams.description: The video, audio, and subtitle streams selected for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision.

SourceSnapshot.description:
The media source characteristics (codecs/streams/protocol) a retained shadow run captured, or
null if none was retained. Never a file path or URL -
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.MediaSourceSnapshot carries none by construction.

Timeline.description:
The lifecycle timeline for this session: `Created`/`Updated` from the session record,
plus (PR113b) any of `FfmpegStarted`/`PlaybackStarted`/`PlaybackStopped` that was
actually observed for it, each stamped with its real, received-at timestamp - never a
fabricated or approximated one. A stage that was never observed is simply absent, not defaulted.

Transforms.description: The pipeline transforms this decision implies.

UpdatedAt.description: When the session was last created or replaced.

PlaybackEngineMode.description:
The role the v2 playback decision engine (`Tesserafin.Playback.Engine`) plays for live playback
(PR115a). This is the single explicit switch a canary rollout moves through; it supersedes the
implicit "shadow on/off" toggle as the statement of intent, while Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Enabled
is kept for backward compatibility (see M:Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.GetEffectiveMode).

AllowAudioStreamCopy.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to allow audio stream copy.

AllowVideoStreamCopy.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable video stream copy.

AlwaysBurnInSubtitleWhenTranscoding.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether always burn in subtitles when transcoding.

AudioStreamIndex.description: Gets or sets the audio stream index.

AutoOpenLiveStream.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to auto open the live stream.

DeviceProfile.description: Gets or sets the device profile.

EnableDirectPlay.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable direct play.

EnableDirectStream.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable direct stream.

EnableTranscoding.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable transcoding.

LiveStreamId.description: Gets or sets the live stream id.

MaxAudioChannels.description: Gets or sets the max audio channels.

MaxStreamingBitrate.description: Gets or sets the max streaming bitrate.

MediaSourceId.description: Gets or sets the media source id.

PlaybackAttemptId.description: Gets or sets the opaque, client-generated playback attempt id (issue #43).

StartTimeTicks.description: Gets or sets the start time in ticks.

SubtitleStreamIndex.description: Gets or sets the subtitle stream index.

UserId.description: Gets or sets the playback userId.

ErrorCode.description: Gets or sets the error code.

MediaSources.description: Gets or sets the media sources.

PlaySessionId.description: Gets or sets the play session identifier.

PlaybackAttemptId.description:
Gets or sets the opaque, client-supplied playback attempt id (issue #43), echoed back
verbatim, or `null` when the client supplied none.

PlaybackLiveFallbackReason.description:
PR115c: why a live playback request fell back to the legacy `StreamInfo` instead of being
served from the v2 Tesserafin.Playback.Execution.PlaybackExecutionPlan, for a session
this server otherwise had an opportunity to serve from v2. Every value here is meant to be
observable (logged and retained for the admin diagnostics surface, mirroring the PR113/PR114
shadow diagnostics pattern) - a fallback must never be silent.

PlaybackLiveWiringOutcome.description:
PR115c: the observable outcome of the live-wiring decision `MediaInfoHelper.SetDeviceSpecificData`
makes for one request - whether the response was actually served from the v2
Tesserafin.Playback.Execution.PlaybackExecutionPlan, or why it fell back to the legacy
`StreamInfo` instead. Retained per session (last decision wins, mirroring
Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.V2PlanRecord's own per-session retention) so the admin diagnostics surface can show
it - see Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.IPlaybackLiveWiringDiagnosticsStore.

FallbackReason.description:
Why legacy was served instead of v2, or null when ServedByV2
is true - a served-by-v2 outcome never carries a fallback reason.

ServedByV2.description:
true when the response was built by M:Tesserafin.Playback.Dlna.PlaybackExecutionPlanAdapter.ToStreamInfo(Tesserafin.Playback.Execution.PlaybackExecutionPlan,Tesserafin.Playback.Execution.PlaybackExecutionContext,Tesserafin.Model.Dto.MediaSourceInfo,Tesserafin.Model.Dlna.DeviceProfile)
            from the v2 plan; false when legacy's own `StreamInfo` was served instead.

PlaybackOperationalMetricsResponse.description:
PR115d: the admin-only operational gate surface for the v2 canary - the response body of
`GET System/PlaybackDiagnostics/Metrics`. Cumulative, cross-session counters
(Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.PlaybackOperationalMetrics) plus the live
stop-threshold guard state (Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.PlaybackStopThresholdGuard) -
deliberately counters only, never session identifiers/paths/URLs, so this can stay a cheap,
dependency-free projection like the sibling Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionListItem.

AdapterAttempts.description:
Live requests that reached the adapter at all - served-by-v2 plus `AdapterError` - the
denominator Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackOperationalMetricsResponse.AdapterErrorRate is computed over.

FallbackReasonCounts.description:
Count of fallback-to-legacy requests, per typed `PlaybackLiveFallbackReason`, keyed by the
enum member's name (not its numeric value) for a stable, readable JSON shape.

ServedByLegacyCount.description: Live requests that fell back to legacy, across every reason.

ServedByV2Count.description: Live requests actually served from the v2 execution plan.

StopThresholdGuardEnabled.description: Whether the guard is enabled in the live configuration right now.

StopThresholdGuardTripped.description:
Whether the guard is forcing legacy for every live request right now - see
Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.PlaybackStopThresholdGuard's remarks: sticky in
practice once tripped, cleared only by an operator config change.

TranscodeStartAttemptsV2.description: Ffmpeg transcode starts observed for v2-served sessions.

TranscodeStartFailureRate.description: Fraction of Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackOperationalMetricsResponse.TranscodeStartAttemptsV2 that failed to start.

TranscodeStartFailuresV2.description: Of those, how many never actually started.

AudioStreamIndex.description: Gets or sets the index of the audio stream.

CanSeek.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this instance can seek.

IsMuted.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this instance is muted.

IsPaused.description: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this instance is paused.

ItemId.description: Gets or sets the item identifier.

LiveStreamId.description: Gets or sets the live stream identifier.

MediaSourceId.description: Gets or sets the media version identifier.

PlayMethod.description: Gets or sets the play method.

PlaySessionId.description: Gets or sets the play session identifier.

PlaybackOrder.description: Gets or sets the playback order.

PositionTicks.description: Gets or sets the position ticks.

RepeatMode.description: Gets or sets the repeat mode.

SessionId.description: Gets or sets the session id.

SubtitleStreamIndex.description: Gets or sets the index of the subtitle stream.

VolumeLevel.description: Gets or sets the volume level.

PlaybackSessionListItem.description:
One row in the admin playback-diagnostics session list (docs/pr92-design-playback-api-and-diagnostics.md
§4.3, PR113): the same stable projection Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponse already exposes,
plus whether a richer diagnostic is available for this session's `{id}` detail route. Never
the internal `Tesserafin.Controller.MediaEncoding.PlaybackSession` record - same rule as the
detail endpoint.

DeviceId.description:
PR114: the requesting client's device identifier, or null under the same
condition as Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionListItem.ItemId. Likewise the raw identifier only - never a resolved device/app
display name.

HasDiagnostic.description:
Whether a retained shadow diagnostic exists for this session - i.e. whether its detail route
would return the v2-sourced fields populated rather than null/empty.

ItemId.description:
PR114: the requested item's identifier, or null when the session was tracked
directly (`IPlaybackSessionManager.Track`) rather than planned from a request, so no
`MediaOptions` was ever attached. Deliberately the raw identifier only - never the resolved
item name/library metadata, which would require this admin-only list to depend on
`ILibraryManager` for what is otherwise a cheap, dependency-free projection.

PlaybackSessionResponse.description:
The stable client-facing playback session response (docs/pr92-design-playback-api-and-diagnostics.md
§4.2): a versioned projection of a playback decision, never the internal
`Tesserafin.Controller.MediaEncoding.PlaybackSession` record. Every property is either a
primitive or drawn from the N:Tesserafin.Playback.Decision vocabulary (PR91) — no
`Tesserafin.Model.Dlna` type (`DeviceProfile`, `MediaOptions`, `StreamInfo`)
ever appears here, so the shape stays stable regardless of which engine produced the decision.

CreatedAt.description: When the session was first created.

DecisionVersion.description:
The version of the decision engine that produced this session's plan. Since PR115a, this is
the real `PlaybackDecision.EngineVersion` when the session's plan authority is v2 (canary
cohort member, or full v2 mode) and this response reflects that decision (see
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponseMapper's
`Map(PlaybackSession, Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.V2PlanRecord?)` overload) — otherwise
it is Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponse.LegacyDecisionVersion, the sentinel for a legacy-projected response.

Kind.description: The kind of media being requested for playback.

Method.description: The method by which the engine decided to deliver a media source to the client.

Output.description: The shape of the output a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision produces.

PlaybackAttemptId.description:
Issue #43. The opaque attempt id the client supplied on the request that created or last
re-planned this session, echoed back verbatim, or null when none was supplied.
Echoing it lets a client confirm the server filed its attempt under the value it meant, and lets
an operator join this response to the client's own trace for the SAME attempt — including across
a retry, where the value is identical while the `RequestId` of issue #42 is not.
Additive and optional: a client that never sends it never sees it, and nothing else changes.

Reasons.description:
A flat summary of the reason codes behind this decision (no technical detail beyond the code
itself, and never a file path, token, or ffmpeg argument). For legacy-sourced sessions, only
the constraint codes that mirror `Tesserafin.Model.Session.TranscodeReason` one-to-one can be
derived — positive/marker codes such as Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonCode.TonemapRequired or
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.ReasonCode.MethodChosen have no legacy reason bit and never appear here.

SelectedStreams.description: The video, audio, and subtitle streams selected for a Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.PlaybackDecision.

Transforms.description:
The pipeline transforms this decision implies. For legacy-sourced sessions this is
best-effort, not read directly off the plan — see

documented approximations.

PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.description:
PR117 (docs/pr116d-url-contract-design.md §2.2): the companion, client-facing descriptor of the
executable URL for a session already planned via `Playback/Sessions` - returned only from
`GET Playback/Sessions/{id}/Stream`, never composed into Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionListItem
or Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackDiagnosticDetail (design doc §1.4: those two reach the admin-elevated,
cross-user diagnostics surface, and a URL there would leak the access token
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.Url carries to any administrator browsing another user's session).

Container.description:
LANE S / issue #44 §8 arbitrage A: the EFFECTIVE output container of the stream
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.Url resolves to - the very value the URL itself carries
(`/stream.{container}` on Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.StreamingProtocol.Http,
`&SegmentContainer={container}` on Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.StreamingProtocol.Hls, where it is
therefore the SEGMENT container, not `m3u8`). Until this field existed the server picked a
container and reported it nowhere, so a client had no way to name what it was about to play
without borrowing the legacy `TranscodingContainer` - which is exactly why reefin-web #24
had to fall the whole remux/non-HLS-transcode decision back to legacy. null
only when the served stream carries no container at all.

FallbackReason.description:
Why legacy was served instead of v2, or null when Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.ServedBy is a
real v2 engine version. Same restricted enum already surfaced on the admin diagnostics detail
route (design doc §2.2/§4).

MimeType.description:
The content type a client should announce to its player for Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.Url, resolved from
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.Container exactly the way the delivery endpoints themselves resolve their own
`Content-Type` header - `application/vnd.apple.mpegurl` on
Tesserafin.Playback.Decision.StreamingProtocol.Hls (the playlist's type, not the segments'), otherwise
`MimeTypes.GetMimeType("." + Container)`, the same call
`VideosController`/`AudioHelper` make on the container they actually write. Reported
rather than re-derived client-side so the announced type can never disagree with the response
the URL will really produce. null when no container is known, or when no
mapping exists for it.

Protocol.description:
The transport protocol an output stream is delivered over. Deliberately neutral vocabulary
(not `Tesserafin.Data.Enums.MediaStreamProtocol` or any other legacy/DLNA type): the domain
depends on nothing outside itself (RFC PR91 §4).

ServedBy.description:
The version of the engine that actually produced Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionStreamDescriptor.Url, resolved at THIS call - same
sentinel as Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackSessionResponse.LegacyDecisionVersion, but deliberately distinct
from the `DecisionVersion` the originating `POST`/`PUT` announced (design doc §3.1:
the two can diverge, this field is authoritative for what is actually served).

SubtitleUrl.description:
The external subtitle delivery URL, present only when the served stream's selected subtitle

Url.description:
The executable URL, resolved at call time - direct output of `StreamInfo.ToUrl(null, accessToken, null)`,
relative (the client already knows its own `baseUrl`, same posture as the legacy
`TranscodingUrl`).

PlaybackShadowOptions.description:
Configures the PR98 shadow mode that dual-runs the v2 playback decision engine
(`Tesserafin.Playback.Engine`) alongside the legacy `StreamBuilder`-based planner for
comparison. Legacy always remains the source of truth for the plan returned to clients,
regardless of these settings; they only control whether/how often/how expensively the shadow
comparison itself runs.

CanaryPercentage.description:
Gets or sets the percentage (0-100) of user/device pairs in the canary cohort when
Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Mode is Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackEngineMode.Canary. Cohort membership is a
deterministic hash of the requesting user and device - the same pair is always in or always
out for a given percentage, never a fresh random draw per request. Clamped to [0, 100] on
set, following this type's PR104 clamp-don't-throw convention. Defaults to 0: enabling
canary mode without choosing a cohort size enrolls nobody.

Enabled.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the shadow comparison runs at all. Defaults to
false: shadow mode is opt-in, since PR100 removed the previous
always-on behavior for safety. PR115a: kept for backward compatibility with configurations
that predate Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Mode - see M:Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.GetEffectiveMode for how the two
combine. New configurations should set Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Mode instead.

MaxExecutionMs.description:
Gets or sets the soft time budget, in milliseconds, for a single shadow execution
(capability/source mapping + v2 engine decision + projection/comparison). Exceeding this
budget is logged and counted; it never cancels or otherwise affects the run in progress,
and never affects the legacy result. PR104: clamped to a minimum of 1 on set - a
zero-or-negative budget would mean "every execution always exceeds budget," which is never
the intent of a misconfigured value.

Mode.description:
Gets or sets the explicit role the v2 engine plays for live playback (PR115a). Defaults to
Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackEngineMode.Legacy. When left at that default, a pre-PR115a
configuration with Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Enabled set still gets shadow behavior - see
M:Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.GetEffectiveMode.

SampleRate.description:
Gets or sets the fraction of eligible playback decisions (0.0-1.0) that actually run the
shadow comparison when Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Enabled is true. 1.0 (the default)
means every decision is shadowed; lower values sample. PR104: clamped to [0, 1] on set - a
value outside that range (including NaN, clamped to 0) has no meaningful sampling
interpretation, so it is corrected rather than left to produce nonsensical behavior
downstream (for example a negative rate always sampling out, or a rate above 1 being
indistinguishable from 1).

StopThresholds.description:
Gets or sets the PR115d operational stop-threshold guard configuration - see
Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackStopThresholdOptions for why this is a sibling type rather than fields
on this class directly. Never null; defaults to a fresh, enabled instance
with its own PR115d defaults, so a configuration that predates PR115d still gets the guard's
protection without needing to add anything.

PlaybackStopThresholdOptions.description:
PR115d: configures the operational stop-threshold guard for the v2 canary - an automatic,
config-driven safety net that forces every live playback request back to legacy (the same
observable effect as the Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Mode kill switch) once the v2 live
path's own error signals cross an operator-chosen threshold, without waiting for a human to
notice and flip the kill switch by hand. A sibling of Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions rather
than a merge into it - Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.StopThresholds holds one instance -
so the two concerns (what role v2 plays; when it auto-disqualifies itself) stay independently
readable and independently testable, matching this configuration surface's existing
one-concern-per-type shape (`TrickplayOptions`, `PlaybackShadowOptions` itself).

AdapterErrorRateThreshold.description:
Gets or sets the fraction (0.0-1.0) of v2-attempted live requests that may end in an
`AdapterError` (`Tesserafin.MediaEncoding.Playback.PlaybackLiveFallbackReason`) before
the guard trips. "v2-attempted" means the request passed every earlier gate (kill switch,
cohort, resolvable plan, source id match, Dolby Vision exclusion) and reached the adapter
(`Tesserafin.Playback.Dlna.PlaybackExecutionPlanAdapter.ToStreamInfo`) - the denominator is
served-by-v2 count plus adapter-error count, not the count of every live request. Not a
`cref` to either type: this project (`Tesserafin.Model`) sits below both in the
dependency graph and must not reference them. Defaults
to 0.10 (10%): the adapter is expected to succeed on essentially every eligible plan (PR115b's
executable-parity invariant exists precisely to make adapter failures rare), so a double-digit
error rate is already a strong signal something is wrong. Clamped to [0, 1] on set, following
this type's PR104 clamp-don't-throw convention.

Enabled.description:
Gets or sets a value indicating whether the stop-threshold guard evaluates at all. Defaults
to true - deliberately the opposite default from Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.Enabled:
PR115d's scope requires the guard to protect production canary traffic by default, with an
operator having to make an explicit, visible choice to turn the safety net off, rather than
having to remember to turn it on.

MinimumSampleSize.description:
Gets or sets the minimum number of samples (v2 attempts, for Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackStopThresholdOptions.AdapterErrorRateThreshold;
v2 transcode starts, for Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackStopThresholdOptions.TranscodeStartFailureRateThreshold) required before a
rate is trusted enough to trip the guard. Defaults to 20: without a floor, the very first v2
request failing would already be a "100% error rate" and would trip the guard on a single
unlucky sample - exactly the kind of premature, noisy trip an operator opening a 1% canary
cohort cannot afford to chase. Clamped to a minimum of 1 on set (mirrors
Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackShadowOptions.MaxExecutionMs's own floor) - zero would make any single
failure trip the guard, which is never the intent of a misconfigured value.

TranscodeStartFailureRateThreshold.description:
Gets or sets the fraction (0.0-1.0) of ffmpeg transcode starts for v2-served sessions that may
fail to actually launch before the guard trips - see `PlaybackOperationalMetrics`'s remarks
for exactly what "failed to start" means and how it is observed
(`ITranscodeManager.TranscodingJobStarted`/`TranscodingJobEnded`). Defaults to 0.20
(20%): transcode start failures have causes entirely outside the v2/legacy decision itself
(disk space, hardware encoder contention, a malformed source), so this threshold is
deliberately looser than Tesserafin.Model.Configuration.PlaybackStopThresholdOptions.AdapterErrorRateThreshold - it exists to catch a v2
plan that is systematically producing FFmpeg arguments ffmpeg cannot start with, not every
transient environmental failure. Clamped to [0, 1] on set, following this type's PR104
clamp-don't-throw convention.

PlaybackAttemptId.description:
Issue #43. Optional, opaque, client-generated. The identifier of the playback ATTEMPT this
request belongs to — generated once by the client when it starts trying to play something, and
resent unchanged on every request of that attempt: `PlaybackInfo`, this `POST`, the
`PUT`, and any retry. A new attempt gets a new value; a retry inside the same attempt keeps
the old one.

Distinct from both neighbouring scopes and substitutable for neither. It is NOT the
`RequestId`/`TraceId` of issue #42, which is server-derived and changes on every
request. It is NOT Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.CreatePlaybackSessionRequest.PlaySessionId, which only exists
once a session does — i.e. after `PlaybackInfo` has already happened — and which survives
across several attempts. See `docs/observabilite-identifiants-correlation.md`.
Diagnostics only: never an authorization key, no access decision is derived from it, and it
replaces no existing access control. Validated for length and printability only (see
Tesserafin.Api.Models.PlaybackSessionDtos.PlaybackAttemptIdValidator); no structure is imposed and no meaning is read out of it.
